analysis.investment_thesis: Helloji Holidays fails both legs of the Magic Formula — a 0.51% ROE implies miserable returns on capital, and an 18.8 P/E translates to an earnings yield of only ~5.3%, below my 6% minimum. This is neither cheap nor a good business, which is the exact opposite of what I look for.
key_strengths: High promoter holding at 69.97% signals skin in the game
Tiny INR 39.4 Cr cap leaves theoretical room to compound if execution improves
Asset-light tour operator model can scale without heavy capex
key_risks: ROE of 0.51% — essentially zero return on capital, fails ROIC filter
Earnings yield ~5.3% (1/18.8) is below attractive threshold of 12%
Micro-cap travel agency with no competitive moat vs MakeMyTrip/Thomas Cook
red_flags: ROE 0.51% — diagnostic of poor capital efficiency
P/E 18.8 on near-zero profitability suggests earnings are a rounding error
Sub-INR 40 Cr BSE micro-cap — liquidity and governance risk
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The Magic Formula ranks companies on two axes: earnings yield (EBIT/EV) and return on capital. Helloji flunks both. An ROE of 0.51% is a flashing red light — even if EBIT/capital is modestly higher than ROE, there is zero chance this business clears my 20%+ ROIC bar. Inverting the P/E gives an earnings yield of roughly 5.3%, well short of the 12% I consider attractive. A business that is neither cheap nor good has no place in a Magic Formula portfolio.

Tour operators are a commoditized, low-moat vertical dominated by larger OTAs and established brands. At INR 39.4 Cr market cap, this is a speculative micro-cap where a single bad quarter can wipe out already-trivial earnings. Until Helloji demonstrates sustained ROIC above 20% for 3+ years AND the earnings yield re-rates above 10%, this is a pass. Score 2/10 — it would be a 1 if not for the meaningful promoter stake.
